name: Mike Rounds

issue_poll.name: SDSU Poll post-election survey of South Dakota registered voters, Nov 13–20, 2020; plus Pew Research Center, July 27–Aug 2, 2020
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–6 from SDSU 'very important' shares, published only by Trump and Biden voters; combined by weighting with the 2020 SD presidential vote (61.8% / 35.6%): economy ~72%, foreign policy ~65%, Supreme Court ~63%, health care ~50%, abortion ~49%, coronavirus ~48%. SDSU asked only those six items, so ranks 7–10 are the next items in Pew's national 'very important' list: violent crime 59%, gun policy 55%, immigration and race/ethnic inequality tied at 52%. Pew source: https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2020/08/13/important-issues-in-the-2020-election/

issues.position: Make the 2017 income tax cuts permanent

votes.question: On the motion to concur in the House amendment

issues.position: Justices who uphold the Constitution; backed Barrett (confirmed pre-term)

issues.note: No Senate floor vote on a government-run health plan this term.

issues.position: Oppose public funding of abortion, including Planned Parenthood

votes.bill_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Planned Parenthood Medicaid cutoff)
votes.question: On passage

issues.position: Shield businesses from COVID lawsuits in relief bills
issues.note: No floor vote on a COVID liability shield found this term.

issues.position: Pass the JUSTICE Act police reform bill
issues.note: No policing reform bill reached a Senate floor vote this term.

issues.position: Oppose further restrictions on gun rights

votes.question: On the motion to concur in the House amendment

issues.position: Increase border security, including border barriers

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

votes.bill_title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (border wall and enforcement funding)
votes.question: On passage

issues.note: S.4361 funded border agents and barrier construction; he opposed it.

caveats: Rounds held no debates in 2020 and Ballotpedia has no issue statement for him; five positions rest on the Christian Coalition's Sept 2020 voter guide, which coded candidates' stances (partly inferred), via OnTheIssues.
Issue ranking combines a small (n=236) post-election SDSU poll reported only by candidate preference with national Pew data.
Immigration S.4361 counted as inconsistent because it included border-security and barrier funding; Republicans opposed it as inadequate.
